AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #20
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why should you wear gloves when handling compost materials? (1 mark)
   A. To make the compost sweeter
   B. So the heap grows faster
   C. To protect your hands from dirt and germs
   D. To keep your hands cold

2. Which of these helps to prevent soil erosion? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving the ground bare
   B. Burning the soil
   C. Covering the ground with mulch or grass
   D. Digging up all the plants

3. Why do we cover a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. To make it heavier
   B. To hide it from animals only
   C. To stop it from rotting
   D. To keep off rain and sun

4. After about how long should the compost heap first be turned? (1 mark)
   A. Two to three weeks
   B. One year
   C. Never
   D. One hour

5. Where is the best place to make a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. In a very windy open road
   B. Inside the kitchen
   C. In the middle of a stream
   D. A shady, well-drained place near the garden

6. Why should the holes in a drip pipe be tiny? (1 mark)
   A. So water pours out fast
   B. So the pipe becomes lighter
   C. So water drips slowly
   D. So the water is warm

7. Where should the holes in the pipe be placed? (1 mark)
   A. Far away from the plants
   B. Next to each plant
   C. Only near the bucket
   D. Only at the end of the row

8. What is the danger of burning charcoal in a closed room? (1 mark)
   A. It gives off a poisonous gas
   B. It makes the room too cold
   C. It creates rain
   D. It makes the walls bigger

9. Why do children need an adult when cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Fuels and fire can burn people
   B. Fire is not dangerous
   C. Children cannot lift a spoon
   D. Adults always cook faster

10. What should you do with the fire when cooking is finished? (1 mark)
   A. Leave it burning
   B. Pour paraffin on it
   C. Add more wood
   D. Put it out

11. Why should a scarecrow be moved every few days? (1 mark)
   A. It gets too hot
   B. It grows
   C. The pole is too heavy
   D. Animals get used to one that never moves

12. Which animal is a domestic animal, not a wild one? (1 mark)
   A. Goat
   B. Monkey
   C. Hare
   D. Squirrel

13. How do you know millet is ready to harvest? (1 mark)
   A. The plant flowers
   B. The plants are green and soft
   C. The seeds are wet
   D. The heads turn brown and the grains are hard

14. What is transplanting? (1 mark)
   A. Harvesting
   B. Making compost
   C. Moving young plants from a nursery to the field
   D. Sowing seeds directly

15. About how far apart may rows of tiny seeds be? (1 mark)
   A. 15 to 20 cm
   B. 5 metres
   C. 10 metres
   D. 1 mm

16. Why should fruit be washed before eating? (1 mark)
   A. To make it dry
   B. To remove dirt and germs
   C. To change its colour
   D. To make it sour

17. Which of these is a climbing fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Grapes
   B. Mango
   C. Orange
   D. Guava

18. What is a fruit? (1 mark)
   A. The stem of a plant
   B. The roots of a plant
   C. The leaves of a plant
   D. The part of a plant that holds the seeds

19. Which is a pest problem for ripe fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Sand
   B. Stones
   C. Fruit flies and birds
   D. Sun

20. Which of these is an animal welfare need? (1 mark)
   A. Living in mud
   B. No shelter
   C. Being hit
   D. Clean water always available

21. Why should a poultry house be clean and dry? (1 mark)
   A. To stop hens from laying
   B. To attract rats
   C. To make eggs blue
   D. To keep birds healthy and safe

22. Why should hands be washed after handling chickens? (1 mark)
   A. To colour the hands
   B. To remove germs
   C. To warm the hands
   D. To get feathers off

23. Which nutrient in eggs helps the body to grow? (1 mark)
   A. Protein
   B. Starch only
   C. Sugar only
   D. Salt

24. Which of these root foods gives the body energy? (1 mark)
   A. Kale
   B. Sweet potato
   C. Egg
   D. Milk

25. Which food is a good source of protein and cheap in many homes? (1 mark)
   A. Sugar
   B. Beans
   C. Soda
   D. Salt

26. Which of these animal foods is rich in protein? (1 mark)
   A. Fish
   B. Cassava
   C. Bread
   D. Banana

27. Which way should pot handles point? (1 mark)
   A. Down into the fire
   B. Inward, away from the edge
   C. Towards children
   D. Outward over the floor

28. Why should food be dry before it is put into hot oil? (1 mark)
   A. Water makes oil colourless
   B. Water makes oil cold
   C. Water makes hot oil splash
   D. Water makes food sweet

29. Which kitchen item helps to turn food in a pan? (1 mark)
   A. A bucket
   B. A spatula
   C. A sieve
   D. A ladle only

30. Which of these is used for boiling food? (1 mark)
   A. A frying pan only
   B. A saucepan with a lid
   C. A basket
   D. A plate

31. Which disease can result from drinking unsafe water? (1 mark)
   A. A cut
   B. Sunburn
   C. Toothache
   D. Cholera

32. How does the tippy tap release water? (1 mark)
   A. By a battery
   B. A foot lever tips the container
   C. By a switch
   D. By a magnet

33. Which PPE protects the body and clothes from dirt? (1 mark)
   A. Dust mask
   B. Gloves
   C. Overall
   D. Canvas shoes

34. What should you do with cleaning materials afterwards? (1 mark)
   A. Drink them
   B. Store them away from small children
   C. Leave them on the floor
   D. Give to animals

35. What should you do if your PPE is damaged? (1 mark)
   A. Keep using it
   B. Hide it
   C. Throw it in a river
   D. Tell a teacher or an adult

36. Why might wet PPE stored away cause a problem? (1 mark)
   A. It becomes cleaner
   B. It grows mould and smells
   C. It becomes lighter
   D. It becomes stronger

37. What should you do after cleaning PPE? (1 mark)
   A. Wipe them on clothes
   B. Wash your hands with soap
   C. Play in mud
   D. Eat without washing

38. How should you hold the cloth if you are right-handed? (1 mark)
   A. Above your head
   B. In the left hand while sewing with the right
   C. Under your foot
   D. In your teeth

39. What should you do at the end of a sewing lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Count the needles and pins
   B. Hide them
   C. Throw them
   D. Leave them

40. Which cloth is easiest for beginners? (1 mark)
   A. Cotton
   B. Wire mesh
   C. Thick leather
   D. Slippery silk

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Describe how to make a scarecrow. (4 marks)

42. Explain four ways in which wild animals help people or the environment. (4 marks)

43. Describe how to wash hands correctly. (4 marks)

44. Choose PPE for gardening and say why. (3 marks)

45. Why do we dust before sweeping? (2 marks)

46. State three safety rules when using needles and scissors. (3 marks)

47. Name three safety rules when using gas for cooking. (3 marks)

48. Plan a group project of making a scarecrow shirt using tacking. Give materials, steps, safety and how the group shares work. (5 marks)

49. Give three ways of caring for a drip irrigation system. (3 marks)

50. Describe how to clean canvas shoes. (4 marks)

51. Plan a weekly cleaning schedule for the classroom using dusting, sweeping, mopping and refuse disposal. (5 marks)

52. Explain how stagnant water around the home can lead to disease and how to prevent it. (4 marks)

53. List three things needed to make a bucket drip system. (3 marks)

54. Explain why it is best to choose fruits that suit your locality. (3 marks)

55. Explain four ways germs can enter the body. (4 marks)

56. Explain three safety rules when cleaning. (3 marks)

57. Name three methods of cleaning the home environment. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #20 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — To protect your hands from dirt and germs
   Gloves protect against germs and cuts.

2. C — Covering the ground with mulch or grass
   Covering keeps rain from washing soil away.

3. D — To keep off rain and sun
   A cover protects the heap from too much rain and drying sun.

4. A — Two to three weeks
   Turning after a few weeks gives air and mixes the heap.

5. D — A shady, well-drained place near the garden
   A shaded, dry spot protects the heap from sun and flooding.

6. C — So water drips slowly
   Small holes give slow drips that soak into the soil.

7. B — Next to each plant
   Water must fall near the roots.

8. A — It gives off a poisonous gas
   Charcoal fumes can make people ill or worse.

9. A — Fuels and fire can burn people
   Adults can guide and help prevent accidents.

10. D — Put it out
   Leaving fire burning wastes fuel and is dangerous.

11. D — Animals get used to one that never moves
   Animals learn that something still is harmless.

12. A — Goat
   Goats are kept by people.

13. D — The heads turn brown and the grains are hard
   Ripe grain is hard and dry.

14. C — Moving young plants from a nursery to the field
   Transplanting means moving seedlings.

15. A — 15 to 20 cm
   Rows are close but leave space for weeding.

16. B — To remove dirt and germs
   Clean fruit is safe to eat.

17. A — Grapes
   Grapes grow on vines.

18. D — The part of a plant that holds the seeds
   Fruits grow from flowers and hold seeds.

19. C — Fruit flies and birds
   Ripe fruit attracts flies and birds.

20. D — Clean water always available
   Animals need water, feed, shelter, health care and kind treatment.

21. D — To keep birds healthy and safe
   Dirty houses spread diseases.

22. B — To remove germs
   Poultry can carry germs.

23. A — Protein
   Eggs are body-building foods.

24. B — Sweet potato
   Sweet potatoes are starchy.

25. B — Beans
   Beans are protein-rich.

26. A — Fish
   Fish is a protein food.

27. B — Inward, away from the edge
   Handles sticking out can be knocked.

28. C — Water makes hot oil splash
   Splashing oil can burn.

29. B — A spatula
   A spatula lifts and turns food.

30. B — A saucepan with a lid
   A saucepan holds water.

31. D — Cholera
   Cholera spreads through dirty water.

32. B — A foot lever tips the container
   Pushing the lever tips the container.

33. C — Overall
   An overall covers the body.

34. B — Store them away from small children
   Keep them safe.

35. D — Tell a teacher or an adult
   Damaged PPE may not protect you.

36. B — It grows mould and smells
   Moulds grow in damp places.

37. B — Wash your hands with soap
   Hands can carry germs.

38. B — In the left hand while sewing with the right
   This is the usual way.

39. A — Count the needles and pins
   Counting ensures none is lost.

40. A — Cotton
   Cotton is easy to handle.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fix a long pole firmly in the ground; tie a shorter stick across it; put a stuffed head on top; dress with a stuffed shirt and hat; add tins or shiny strips.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Birds eat insects; bees pollinate; animals spread seeds; wildlife brings tourists and money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Wet hands; use soap; rub palms, backs of hands, between fingers, thumbs and nails for about 20 seconds; rinse; dry with a clean cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Gloves protect hands from dirt and cuts; gumboots protect feet from mud; hat protects the head from the sun.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item with reason.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Dust falls to the floor, so sweeping afterwards removes it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dust falls, 1 mark for sweeping removes.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Never put needles in the mouth; keep them in a pin cushion; count them; carry scissors with points down (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Keep the cylinder upright and away from fire; close the valve after use; if you smell gas open windows and do not light a flame.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

48. (5 marks)
   Answer: Materials: old cloth, needles, thread, scissors, chalk, ruler. Steps: measure and cut two pieces; pin; tack along sides; leave openings; sew firmly; stuff. Safety: count needles. Group: share tools, assign jobs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark materials, 2 marks steps, 1 mark safety, 1 mark teamwork.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fill the container daily, check for leaks and blocked holes, keep the water covered and clean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Remove laces; brush off loose dirt; scrub gently with soapy water; rinse; stuff with paper; dry in the shade.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

51. (5 marks)
   Answer: A table of days with jobs for each learner group: Monday dusting, Tuesday sweeping, Wednesday mopping, and refuse disposal each day, with tools and safety measures.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for jobs, 1 for tools, 1 for safety, 1 for fairness of sharing.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mosquitoes breed in it and spread malaria. Empty tins and tyres, fill puddles, and drain water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for breeding, 1 mark for disease, 2 marks for prevention.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: A bucket or container, a hose or pipe, and small holes or drippers for water to come out. A stand may also be used.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: They grow better in the local climate, give more fruit, and need less care and cost.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

55. (4 marks)
   Answer: Through the mouth from dirty hands, dirty food, dirty water, and through cuts or feet without shoes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not mix chemicals; keep chemicals from children; wear gloves for dirty work; do not leave floors wet (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sweeping, dusting, mopping and disposal of refuse (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each method.
